‘The Yemeni Armed Forces have become so powerful that we are now dictating terms. With God's help, we have established three principles: 
First, a blockade for a blockade, whereby we have imposed a strict siege on the Saudi enemy, preventing even a single ship from passing through. Second, striking Saudi troop concentrations wherever they may be. Third, protecting Yemen's sovereignty and confronting any enemy airspace incursions. 
In implementing this blockade for a blockade, from the declaration of the maritime embargo against the Saudi enemy on July 20th until today, the Yemeni Armed Forces have targeted eight Saudi oil tankers: five in the Red Sea and three in the Gulf of Aden and the Arabian Sea. 
Additionally, 48 Saudi oil tankers were prevented from passing and forced to turn back, including 34 in the Arabian Sea and the Indian Ocean, and 14 in the Red Sea. 
In response to the Saudi aggression against Sana'a Airport and Hodeidah Port, and to reinforce the principle of protecting Yemeni sovereignty from violations of our country's airspace, particularly in the governorates of Sa'dah and Hajjah, the Yemeni Armed Forces carried out nine military operations targeting Yanbu, Najran, Jizan, Abha, and oil supply lines in the Eastern Province. 
Furthermore, to solidify the principle of targeting Saudi troop concentrations wherever they may be, the Armed Forces conducted fourteen military operations targeting Saudi enemy troop concentrations in Al-Ruwaik, Al-Abr, Al-Wadi'ah, Ma'rib, and Al-Mukha, as well as ships and boats transporting equipment and reinforcements belonging to the Saudi enemy. 
The results of these operations included the death and injury of hundreds of Saudi enemy troops, including commanders and officers; the burning and destruction of a large number of warehouses and equipment belonging to the Saudi enemy; the sinking and burning of two military landing ships transporting Saudi weapons and reinforcements in Al-Mukha; the burning and sinking of more than ten ships belonging to the Saudi enemy, which were engaged in acts of piracy, banditry, and looting in the Red Sea under Saudi directives. 
We warn the Saudi regime against the dangers of any escalation. Any escalation will be met with a comprehensive response. The Saudi regime has no option but to lift the blockade, implement the agreements reached, end the aggression, pay salaries, allow the occupiers to leave, and return the wealth of the Yemeni people to all of us. We advise those of our countrymen who have been misled to return and leave the enemy camps, because they are Yemenis, and we do not want to target them or make them victims.’

🇪🇺🇺🇸🇷🇺 NATO has developed a plan for ground combat operations in the event of a large-scale Russian attack on Alliance countries
– Bild.
NATO's first task is to suppress missile strikes. Fighters, missiles and drones will be deployed to disable Russian missile systems.
One of the targets is the Kaliningrad region, where Russia has stationed a significant number of anti-aircraft and missile systems.
Simultaneously, on the borders with Russia and Belarus, NATO plans to create a so-called "autonomous zone."
It is meant to serve as a protective barrier between Russian forces and those of the North Atlantic Alliance.
In this zone, drones and unmanned military vehicles should operate primarily.
NATO military personnel should not be stationed there.
If Russian troops continue their offensive, unmanned systems are to be used to deter and stop them.
The next stage could involve striking targets already on Russian territory.
This refers to military-logistical infrastructure supplying Russian forces. Targets include airfields, military factories, bridges and railways used to transport troops and materiel to the front.
The Alliance also plans to rely on Russians who are opposed to the authorities.
A separate element of the plan is the creation of an "air bridge." Through it, aircraft are to deliver drones and robotic systems into Russia, which could be used to destroy military bases and airfields.
At the same time, the concept notes: NATO does not aim to conquer Russia. The goal is to stop and push back advancing Russian troops to Russia's borders.

🪖🇪🇺NATO’s Saber Junction drills: more saber-rattling or prelude to outright attack on Russia?
 
The Western alliance has kicked off its Saber Junction-2026 drills - large-scale “combat readiness exercises” in Hohenfels, Germany led by US Army Europe and Africa command and including participants from 11 nations, including eight NATO members, Bosnia, Kosovo and Ukraine.
👉 Ukraine has been given special “partner nation” status, focused on interoperability, algorithmic warfare (testing AI in command functions and trying to accelerate the ‘detect-to-kill’ cycle using real-world datasets) and counter-drone strategies (again based on real-world experience).
Involving close to 5.5k troops, the drills promise to test brigade-level readiness “for multi-domain operations and large-scale ground combat scenarios,” practice rapid deployment, including of Airborne “sky soldiers,” and drill in both defensive and offensive maneuvers.
🪖 The drills’ include operational testing and validation of the so-called “Eastern Flank Deterrence Initiative,” a concept aimed at “operationalizing” the alliance’s planning in Eastern Europe using “data-driven, high-tech land warfare.”
In other words, preparation for the next war against Russia.
➡️ At a NATO defense ministerial meeting in Brussels in June, Pete Hegseth called NATO a “paper tiger” and demanded that it be transformed “back into a real military alliance that’s focused on hard power and real deterrence,” modelled on the alliance’s 20th century mission and capabilities, but with more contributions from European allies.
The problem with that vision is that the “NATO 1.0” minus the US Hegseth harkens back to had only one mission: to fight Russia in the heart of Europe.
❗️ The US and their European allies have already done a great job sacrificing Ukraine at the altar of a proxy conflict against Moscow. Now, NATO seems set on escalating the stakes to include the Europeans themselves.
Saber Junction-2026 is just one of half-a-dozen major NATO drills already held this year, from Steadfast Dart (January-March, ~10k troops) to Cold Response (March, 32k personnel), AURORA (April-May, 18k troops), Sword (April-May, 15.5k troops), and BALTOPS (June, 6k troops, 20 warships).
Clearly, Russia wants war. Look how close they put their country next to all our military bases and exercises.
